title: Candidate result
description: Generator or Researcher to Coordinator. Always a candidate: this packet proposes, admission disposes. It is structurally incapable of asserting an accepted status — candidate_status has no VERIFIED member, because a role that could accept its own work would make every other rule in the frame decorative.

target_sha256.description: Must equal the work item's. A mismatch is disqualifying, not a penalty to weigh against other merits.

trust_boundary.description: Fixed. Present so no consumer can mistake this packet for an admission.

candidate_status.description: The strongest status this result CLAIMS, pending admission. VERIFIED is deliberately absent. SUPERSEDED means it lost a race to a sibling — not refuted, and never recorded as a failure.

dependency_path_to_target.description: Required for any product proposed for acceptance. A checked sub-result that cannot be traced to the target is not progress toward it.

receipt_ref.description: Hash-bound, not a bare pointer: an unbound reference survives the receipt it names being re-run to a different verdict.

fidelity_record.description: Whether the artifact faithfully encodes the frozen claim. A separate gate from verification: the backend proves things about the encoding, not about whether the encoding says what the target says. Missing is an error; false is a demotion.

checked_by_ref.description: Opaque actor handle. Must differ from the result's emitter — self-certified fidelity is not fidelity.

evidence.description: At least one entry for any status above CONJECTURE.

bounds.description: Required for bounded_search. The stated finite domain actually searched — outside it, the search establishes nothing.

target_sha256.description: Echoed on every item so evidence harvested from a neighbouring claim is detectable without dereferencing it.

as_hard_as_target.description: True ends the escalation. Say so rather than continuing to spend against it.

failure_record.description: Required when candidate_status is FAILED_ATTEMPT or REJECTED. Written when the failure occurred, not reconstructed at synthesis.

diagnostic.description: Backend or checker evidence, not a paraphrase of it.

revival_condition.description: What would make this worth retrying. A block with no revival condition throws away the reason it was blocked; most dead routes are dead only conditional on current knowledge.

failure_signature.description: How this domain identifies 'the same failure'. Required so the repeated-signature escalation trigger is evaluable rather than aspirational.

closure_audit.description: Required for PARTIAL or CONDITIONAL. Absent means automatic demotion — this is the anti-overclaiming core.

repeated_observation.description: True forces zero gain. Old evidence relabelled as new is not information.

next_mutation.description: The single axis worth changing next. A failure with no proposed next move under-delivers.

payload_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of this packet with payload_sha256 removed: sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII escapes. Seals the packet and makes it addressable by later packets — an id alone is a mutable label.

work_item_sha256.description: Seal of the work item this answers. target_sha256 does not cover the dispatch constraints — tier, forbidden_drift, stop_rule — so a work item re-issued under the same id with looser constraints would otherwise still validate.

reuse.description: Whether this result came from cache rather than fresh work. A cache hit is evidence about checkability, never about truth: it orders work, it does not confer status.

context_match_axes.description: Every axis on which the cached context matched. Reuse is legitimate only when all declared axes match.

method_family.description: The approach family this result came from. Compared against a reviewer's method_family when the reviewer shares the producer's role: same role and same family is one check performed twice.

actor.description: Who executed this packet, as the orchestrator sees it. The frame cannot verify identity — sessions, workers and processes belong to the orchestrator — so it records what was attested and refuses to treat an unattested separation as a demonstrated one. Two packets sharing an actor_id are the same actor whatever their role labels say.

actor_id.description: Opaque, orchestrator-assigned. Stable within a run.

attested_by.description: `orchestrator` means something outside the run vouched that this actor is distinct. `self`, or an absent actor block, means nobody did — independence is then NOT_RUN, which puts CONDITIONAL and VERIFIED out of reach.

attestation_ref.description: Optional orchestrator-side handle for the attestation.

obligations_answered.description: One entry per obligation the work item carried. `not_done` is a legitimate answer and an honest one — what is refused is silence, because a step nobody mentions and a step nobody took are indistinguishable in a result.
